short: The surfaces and feedback pieces, their shapes and mints
is: Where the surfaces and the feedback pieces live with the plain shapes they take and their run-time choices. Today it holds Card, Badge, Spinner, Skeleton, VisibilityMarker and StatusPill, all simple, with `types.ts` (their shapes and `FeedbackAction`) and `choices.ts` (the allow-lists each piece falls back through).
conventions: Each piece is simple or composite, as `src/checks/composition-table.ts` says. A simple piece draws its own element and its own family class and holds only glyphs and the internal pieces; a composite lays out library components with its own family class and plain text, and draws no button, link, field or picture of its own: an action is a `FeedbackAction` handed to Button.

One `.svelte` file per piece, its `X.svelte.spec.ts` beside it, and its stories under `src/stories/` tagged with its kind. Shapes and mints are plain TypeScript next to the pieces, readonly, with a `kind` discriminant and `?: never` on the keys another form owns.

A piece's looks are its family stylesheet in `../styles/surfaces`, whose selectors name only its own families; it writes no colour, time or size of its own, and moves only through the seam, like the controls.
Everything the library's conventions say holds here: dumb, controlled, every word a prop, no type from bits-ui or the date library passed out.

fs.name: Badge.svelte
fs.role: a small tag with a label, one of six tones and an optional icon

fs.name: Card.svelte
fs.role: a sheet for one object: a div, section, article or li chosen from a closed map, with or without padding; it holds whatever it is given

fs.name: Skeleton.svelte
fs.role: a blank in the shape of what is coming: text lines (the last one shorter), a rectangle or a circle; hidden from screen readers and breathing through the seam

fs.name: Spinner.svelte
fs.role: a ring that turns through the seam: a status with its words, or the glyph alone (what Button's busy state will hold)

fs.name: StatusPill.svelte
fs.role: a pill of one or two parts, each with a label, tone and optional icon, and a quiet fact beside it

fs.name: VisibilityMarker.svelte
fs.role: who can see a thing: an icon and the word for private, listed or public, or the icon alone with its word read out once

fs.name: choices.ts
fs.role: the run-time choices, each taking any value and falling back to the safe one: the card element, the badge and status tones, the visibility level and its icon, an icon name and the number of skeleton lines

fs.name: types.ts
fs.role: `FeedbackAction`, and the shapes of the surfaces: the card element and padding, the badge and status tones, a status pill's parts and fact, the visibility levels and their words
